facts: Q1 2026 net revenue was $722 million, down 7% year-over-year from $776 million, with core revenue declining 10%.
Q1 adjusted EBITDA fell 72% year-over-year to $6 million with margin of 0.9%, down 190 basis points.
Net debt leverage rose to 11.3x at the end of Q1, and the company drew $40 million on its revolver to fund a $43 million working capital use and $91 million operating cash outflow.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $3.05–$3.20 billion (from $2.95–$3.10 billion), implying core revenue decline of 3%–6% versus the prior 5%–10%.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained at $100–$150 million, with operating cash flow of ~$40 million, free cash flow use of ~$60 million, and capex of ~$100 million.

In the 2026 EBITDA bridge, expected net share loss headwind was reduced to $30 million from $60 million, while price/cost headwind worsened to $40 million from $10 million due to freight inflation and competitive/promotional pricing.

North America Q1 revenue declined to $453 million from $531 million, with adjusted EBITDA dropping to $4 million (0.8% margin) from $16 million (2.9% margin), reflecting volume losses and the Towanda divestiture.
Europe Q1 revenue rose 10% to $269 million aided by ~11.5 points of FX tailwind, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $7 million (2.6% margin) from $11 million (4.3% margin).
On-Time, In-Full delivery rates improved to over 90%, with management targeting consistent operation above 95%, and April sales tracked in line with expectations supporting the improved outlook.

Management expects Q2 EBITDA ramp (implied ~$31 million at the midpoint) driven by seasonality and Q1 pricing actions flowing through, and continues a strategic review of the European business while evaluating asset sales and sale-leasebacks to address near-term maturities before they go current in December.
Delek US reported a Q1 2026 net loss of $201 million or $3.34 per share, with adjusted net income of approximately $5 million ($0.08 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $212 million.
Excluding Small Refinery Exemptions, Q1 adjusted EBITDA was approximately $129 million with an adjusted loss of $0.98 per share, removing an $82 million RVO exemption recognition benefit.
The company raised its Enterprise Optimization Plan (EOP) target to at least $220 million on an annual run-rate basis, with approximately $60 million of EOP contribution recognized in Q1 2026.
Big Spring refinery completed its planned turnaround safely, on budget, and on time, with no further turnarounds or major capital projects planned for the remainder of 2026.

Q2 2026 throughput guidance totals 293,000–313,000 bpd system-wide (Tyler 72-77k, El Dorado 78-83k, Big Spring 65-70k, Krotz Springs 78-83k), with Big Spring guidance described as conservative post-turnaround.
Q2 2026 guidance includes operating expenses of $215-225 million, G&A of $47-52 million, D&A of $105-115 million, and net interest expense of $80-90 million.

Delek Logistics (DKL) reaffirmed 2026 EBITDA guidance of $520-560 million, generated approximately $132 million in Q1 logistics EBITDA (including a ~$10 million negative impact from winter storm Fern), and is expected to exceed 80% third-party EBITDA on a pro forma basis in 2026.

Q1 capital spending was $181 million at Delek stand-alone (mostly Big Spring turnaround) plus $50 million at DKL (~$42 million growth), while cash from operations was $461 million and financing used $273 million including $16 million in dividends.
Supply and Marketing posted a Q1 loss of approximately $61 million (wholesale marketing -$27.1M, asphalt -$12.1M, supply remainder), described as timing impacts that will reverse over time.

Management estimates a 2026 RVO compliance obligation of approximately $750 million at a $1.50/gallon blended RIN price (though current RINs are ~$1.90), and sees mid-cycle free cash flow potential of $600-700 million, representing 20-30% of current market cap.
Q3 2025 EBITDA was negative $28 million, including a $20 million noncash inventory impairment, compared to negative EBITDA of $21 million in Q2.

Lower pulp sales realizations negatively impacted EBITDA by approximately $15 million, with the inventory impairment split as approximately $15 million attributed to hardwood and the remainder to softwood.
U.S. dollar weakness increased operating costs by almost $11 million compared to Q2 2025.
The company expects to realize approximately $30 million in cost savings and reliability improvements by the end of 2025 through its One Goal One Hundred program.
Liquidity position at end of Q3 totaled $376 million, comprised of approximately $98 million of cash and $278 million of undrawn revolvers.
Q3 cash consumption was approximately $48 million compared to $35 million in Q2, driven primarily by lower EBITDA.
The company's mass timber backlog of projects sits at about $80 million, with potential sales volumes from project inquiries in the last two quarters totaling approximately $400 million.
Planned 2025 CapEx spend is about $100 million, with 2026 CapEx expected to start around $75 million as the company prioritizes liquidity.
Canadian lumber now faces total duty and tariff impact of approximately 50% on average following Section 232 review, compared to 10% for European lumber.
The NBSK net price in China was $690 per tonne in Q3, a decrease of $44 from Q2, while North American NBSK list price averaged $1,700 per tonne, down $120 from the prior quarter.
Q4 2025 revenue came at the high end of guidance at $7.3 million, down from $10.1 million in Q3, and the company believes Q4 represented the revenue bottom.
High-power markets represented the majority of total revenue for the first time in Q4, while Mobile declined to less than 25% of revenue and is expected to become insignificant by end of 2026.
Q1 2026 revenue is guided to $8 million to $8.5 million with gross margin of 38.7% plus or minus 25 basis points, representing the first quarter-over-quarter growth since the company's pivot.
The company completed a private placement of common stock in November 2025 with net proceeds of approximately $96 million, contributing to a quarter-end cash balance of $237 million with no debt.
Full year 2025 revenue was $45.9 million compared to $83.3 million in 2024, with full year gross margin of 38.4% versus 40.4% last year.

The company executed a 19% workforce reduction in Q4 and consolidated distribution channel partners from approximately 40 to fewer than 10, with operating expenses targeted to remain flat at approximately $15 million per quarter throughout 2026.

Q4 GAAP results included a $16.6 million restructuring and impairment charge consisting of approximately $10 million in distribution contract terminations, $4 million in fixed asset impairments, and $2 million in workforce reduction expenses.
The company's serviceable addressable market is projected at $3.5 billion by 2030, split roughly 50-50 between GaN and high-voltage SiC, with a combined CAGR of more than 60%.

The company announced a long-term strategic technology and manufacturing partnership with GlobalFoundries to accelerate GaN design and manufacturing in the U.S., with production expected to begin later in the year and accelerate in 2027.
CFO Todd Glickman announced his departure after 10 years of service, with a successor expected to be communicated in the coming weeks.
Q1 2026 total revenues were $572 million, up 8% year-over-year, while recurring and other revenue grew 9% year-over-year to $544 million.
GAAP net income was $156 million ($3.04 per diluted share) and non-GAAP net income was $161 million ($3.15 per diluted share) on 51 million diluted shares.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $275 million, expanding 50 basis points year-over-year to a 48.2% margin.

Paycom repurchased approximately 8.4 million shares (about 15% of shares outstanding as of year-end 2025) for $1.06 billion during Q1, and the board approved a new $2 billion buyback authorization on May 4 to replace the prior one.
The company paid approximately $18 million in cash dividends in Q1 and declared a next quarterly dividend of $0.375 per share, payable in early June.
In April, Paycom replaced its revolver with a new 5-year, $2.125 billion credit facility, of which $675 million is currently drawn.

Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed: total revenue of $2.175–$2.195 billion (~6.5% growth at midpoint), recurring and other revenue growth of 7%–8%, and adjusted EBITDA of $950–$970 million (~44% margin at midpoint), including ~$103 million of interest on funds held for clients.
Average daily balance on funds held for clients was approximately $3.1 billion in Q1, up 8% year-over-year, and cash and cash equivalents ended the quarter at $154 million.
IWant AI usage has grown another 33% since the end of Q4 2025, and the tool is included free with the system rather than monetized separately.

Management stated Paycom serves approximately 5% of its addressable market, indicated Q1 bookings came in on budget after a 3-month sales retraining initiative, and noted client revenue retention increased in 2025 with Net Promoter Score continuing to rise.

Heron generated approximately $155 million in total net revenues for full year 2025 and delivered adjusted EBITDA of $14.7 million, exceeding the previously communicated guidance range of $9 million to $13 million.
Full year 2025 gross margin was approximately 73%, reflecting continued improvements in cost discipline and product mix.
In Q4 2025, ZYNRELEF delivered 48% net revenue growth year-over-year while APONVIE grew 97% year-over-year, with the overall Acute Care franchise increasing more than 57% year-over-year.

Acute Care net sales were $16.3 million in Q4, up 33% from $12.3 million in Q3, with ZYNRELEF net sales increasing to $12.5 million from $9.3 million and APONVIE rising to $3.8 million from $3 million.

The Oncology franchise generated just over $105 million in net revenue for full year 2025, representing a 7.8% decline compared to 2024, with the majority attributable to the planned wind-down of SUSTOL throughout 2026.

Heron's 2026 guidance projects net product sales of $173 million to $183 million and adjusted EBITDA of $10 million to $20 million, with the company planning targeted commercial investments that may temper near-term EBITDA expansion.

The prefilled syringe presentation for ZYNRELEF had registration batches placed on stability in Q4 2025, requiring 12 months of stability testing before filing, with potential FDA approval targeted for mid- to late 2027.
APONVIE demand units grew 101% year-over-year and received a permanent product-specific J-Code (J8502) as well as inclusion in the newly released Fifth Consensus Guidelines for management of PONV.

Management expects the CINV franchise sales to stay relatively flat in 2026, with unit volume growth from hospital promotion offset by price erosion, and the Slayback litigation decision is expected before the 30-month stay expires.

The company plans to begin adding field sales capacity midyear 2026, targeted to priority geographies with strong access, reimbursement, and distributor traction, representing increased commercial investment to accelerate revenue growth.

Compass raised its cost synergy targets to $300 million actioned by end of year 1 (up from $250 million) and $500 million net over 3 years (up from $400 million), with $420 million through the P&L and $80 million as CapEx synergies.
2026 in-year realized cost synergies were doubled from approximately $100 million to $200 million, with $130 million flowing through the P&L (up from $40 million) and $70 million as CapEx savings.
Q1 2026 pro forma revenue was $2.76 billion, up 7% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $61 million—a record Q1 result, exceeding the $15-$35 million guidance range by a wide margin.

Q1 adjusted EBITDA benefited from a $19 million favorable LTIP mark-to-market adjustment tied to Compass' stock price decline; excluding this, adjusted EBITDA would have been $42 million, still above guidance.
Q2 2026 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of $4.0-$4.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $310-$350 million, with full-year non-GAAP OpEx expected at $2.7-$2.75 billion.

Management provided scenario analysis showing the combined company could generate ~$1 billion adjusted EBITDA / $750 million unlevered FCF at trough 4.1M existing home sales, scaling to $2.5 billion EBITDA / ~$2 billion FCF at 6M home sales.
Compass plans to redeem the full $500 million of 9.75% notes when first callable on April 15, 2027, paying a $25 million redemption premium to save nearly $50 million in annual interest expense.

Pro forma brokerage GTV grew 7.3% year-over-year versus the market at 1.5%, marking 20 consecutive quarters of organic market outperformance, while pro forma integrated services revenue grew 11% with refi transactions up 100%.

Q1 free cash flow was negative $168 million due to Anywhere transaction costs, but cash ended at $484 million (up $285 million) aided by $880 million in net convert proceeds; Q2 may be near breakeven to slightly negative FCF.

Approximately 56% of agents shed in Q1 had zero GCI production and another 21% had $20,000 or less in trailing 12-month GCI; excluding these, pro forma agent retention was 97-98%, and Compass recruited more principal agents than any prior Q1 in its history.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $66.8 million was up 10% year-over-year, at the top end of the company's 5% to 10% guidance range.
Q3 free cash flow was $66.7 million, more than double the $24.7 million generated in Q3 2024, and year-to-date free cash flow of $85 million has already doubled full year 2024 levels.
SAS adjusted EBITDA margin reached 15.3% in Q3, up 200 basis points year-over-year and the strongest since the merger.
FAM segment achieved its first quarter of growth in sales and adjusted EBITDA since the merger, with sales of $198 million up 4% year-over-year.
Net debt was reduced by more than $60 million versus last quarter to $932 million, bringing the net leverage ratio to 4.2x with expectations to approach 4x by year-end.
The company is targeting $35 million to $40 million of cost savings by year-end 2026, with $15 million to $20 million expected to be realized in 2025.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase by at least 10% versus the prior year period.
Less than 6% of annual sales are currently subject to tariffs, improved from the previous guidance of 7%.
Adjusted EPS increased to $0.39 per share in Q3 compared to $0.21 per share in the prior year period.

The company has reduced its global site footprint to 34 facilities from 48 at the time of the merger, with the Wilson, North Carolina facility closure expected to be accretive to earnings starting in Q1 2026.
Q4 2025 diluted EPS of $0.89 exceeded analyst consensus of $0.88 and represented a 7% increase compared to the linked quarter.
Full year 2025 loan growth reached 6% compared to 2024, hitting the top end of prior guidance.
Net interest margin guidance for full year 2026 is between 4% and 4.2%, with each 25 basis point Fed rate cut expected to reduce NIM by 3 to 4 basis points.
High balance leases in the small ticket leasing business were reduced from $35 million at end of 2024 to $13 million at year-end 2025.
Management expects net charge-offs to remain elevated in the first half of 2026 and begin to taper off in the second half of 2026.
The company expects to cross $10 billion in assets in 2027 absent any actions but has no plans to cross that threshold organically.
Quarterly noninterest expense is expected to range between $72 million and $74 million for Q2-Q4 2026, with Q1 being higher due to annual expenses.
Tangible book value per share improved 3% to $22.77, while book value per share grew 2% to $33.78.
Subordinated debt redemption will result in annual savings of approximately $1 million with a tangible book value earn-back period of less than 1 year.
2026 loan growth is expected to be between 3% and 5% compared to 2025, dependent on timing of paydowns and payoffs.
LKQ completed the sale of its Self Service segment to Pacific Avenue Capital Partners for $410 million, with proceeds used to reduce debt.
The company achieved $35 million in cost savings in Q3, on track to meet its $75 million cost savings target for 2025.
Full year 2025 adjusted diluted EPS guidance was narrowed to $3.00-$3.15, with the midpoint raised by $0.07 on a like-for-like basis after adjusting for the Self Service sale.
Free cash flow was $387 million in Q3, bringing year-to-date free cash flow to $573 million.
The Specialty segment delivered 9.4% organic revenue growth, marking the first positive organic growth in 14 quarters.
Wholesale North America revenue decreased by only 30 basis points per day, outperforming repairable claims decline of approximately 6% by nearly 600 basis points.
Europe segment EBITDA margin was 10.0%, representing a 60 basis point sequential improvement from Q2 despite a 4.7% organic revenue decline per day.
Wholesale North America segment EBITDA margin was 14.0%, a 180 basis point decrease versus the prior year due to tariff-related pricing pressures and unfavorable customer mix.
Total debt was $4.2 billion with a leverage ratio of 2.5x EBITDA as of September 30, with an additional $390 million repaid on October 1 from Self Service sale proceeds.
The company returned $118 million to shareholders in Q3, including $40 million to repurchase 1.2 million shares and $78 million for quarterly dividends.
RingCentral generated record free cash flow of over $530 million in 2025, up 32% year-over-year, translating to $5.81 of free cash flow per share (up 36% YoY).
The company announced its first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.075 per share and a $250 million increase in share repurchase authorization, bringing total buyback authorization to $500 million.

ARR from customers utilizing at least one monetized AI product (RCAI utilizing customers) more than doubled year-over-year and now approaches 10% of overall ARR, with net retention rates exceeding 100%.
The value of new equity grants declined 36% year-over-year to approximately $160 million (6% of revenue), with a steady-state SBC target of 3%-4% of revenue in the next 3-4 years.
Full year 2025 GAAP operating margin reached 4.8%, with management expecting it to approximately double to ~9% in 2026 and targeting ~20% GAAP operating margin in the next 3-4 years.
AI Receptionist (AIR) customer count reached 8,300 in Q4, up 44% sequentially, while ACE customer count exceeded 4,800, up 144% year-over-year.
Small business and global service provider segments, totaling over $1.1 billion in combined ARR, both grew in double digits and performed well above the Rule of 40.
For full year 2026, the company guided subscription revenue growth of 4.5%-5.5%, free cash flow of $580-$600 million (up 11% at midpoint), and non-GAAP EPS of $4.76-$4.97 (up 11% at midpoint).
RingCX was adopted by more than 1,500 customers (nearly doubling YoY) with revenue and ARR more than doubling, and over half of $1 million-plus TCV deals in Q4 included RingCX.
The company plans to use its $955 million undrawn credit facility to address the $609 million convertible note maturing in March 2026, after which there are no debt maturities until 2030.
Q1 2026 net sales were approximately $592 million, up 1.1% reported but down 4.2% on a currency-neutral basis versus Q1 2025.
The Middle East conflict caused an $11 million revenue impact in Q1, with the region representing over 9% of the Diagnostics segment in 2025 and being one of Bio-Rad's fastest-growing markets.
Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered to currency-neutral revenue growth of -3% to +0.5%, with Life Science at -3% to -1% and Diagnostics at -3% to +1%.

Non-GAAP operating margin guidance for full-year 2026 was set at 10%-12%, with non-GAAP gross margin projected at 53%-54%, and Q1 non-GAAP operating margin came in at just 6.6% versus 10.8% a year ago.
Non-GAAP EPS was $1.89 in Q1 2026, down from $2.54 in Q1 2025, while the Sartorius equity stake fair value change drove a reported net loss of $527 million, or $19.55 per diluted share.
ddPCR instrument revenue grew 24% year-over-year in Q1, but ddPCR consumables were down low double digits, leaving the total ddPCR portfolio essentially flat.

Process chromatography revenue declined 13% year-over-year on a currency-neutral basis in Q1, with management reiterating expectations for a low-single-digit recovery in 2027 toward a mid-single-digit longer-term trajectory.
Full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance was reduced to $290 million-$340 million, with Q1 free cash flow of $78 million versus $96 million in Q1 2025.
Bio-Rad repurchased 176,000 shares for approximately $48 million in Q1 2026, with about $237 million remaining under the current buyback authorization.

Management shifted M&A focus toward revenue- and margin-generating targets in the $100 million-$500 million revenue range, away from early-stage opportunities, and reiterated a near-term goal of mid-teens operating margin.
Apollo generated record combined fee and spread related earnings which drove adjusted net income of $1.4 billion or $2.17 per share, up 17% year-over-year in Q3 2025.
Fee-related earnings (FRE) of $652 million was up 23% year-over-year, with management fee growth of 22% year-over-year.
Record AUM reached $908 billion at quarter end, up 24% year-over-year, with fee-generating AUM of $685 billion.
Q3 origination was $75 billion at an average spread of 350 basis points over treasuries, the second strongest quarter following a record Q2, bringing LTM origination to over $270 billion.
Apollo expects Q4 SRE of approximately $880 million, driving estimated full year SRE of $3.475 billion, approximately 8% year-over-year growth above the mid-single-digit target.
Athene's net invested assets grew 18% year-over-year to $286 billion with $23 billion of organic inflows in Q3, including $10 billion from retail and $10 billion from funding agreements.
Global wealth channel raised $5 billion in Q3, its second-best quarter on record, bringing year-to-date total to over $14 billion, up 60% over the prior year period.
Apollo expects FRE growth of 20% plus in 2026 in addition to earnings from Bridge, with approximately 75% of top line growth attributable to existing businesses.
Athene reduced its floating rate sensitivity significantly, with SRE sensitivity from a 25 basis point move in short-term rates now approximately $10-15 million versus $30-40 million previously.
Apollo executed over $350 million in share repurchases during Q3, with the majority being opportunistic.
Q1 2026 total revenue was $3.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year, with Pharmacy Solutions revenue of $3.2 billion (+25%) and Provider Services revenue of $442 million (+28%).
Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA grew 45% to $190 million with margin expanding ~70 bps to 5.3%, and adjusted EPS was $0.39.

Full-year 2026 guidance was updated to revenue of $14.725B–$15.225B (14.1%–17.9% growth ex-Community Living) and adjusted EBITDA of $795M–$825M (28.7%–33.6% growth), including ~$30M EBITDA from the Amedisys/LHC acquired branches.
BrightSpring completed the divestiture of Community Living to Sevita on March 30, 2026 for ~$811M net cash proceeds (gross $835M), with ~$100M in taxes payable in Q2.

Leverage declined to 2.27x as of March 31, 2026 (2.40x pro forma for Community Living taxes) from 2.99x at year-end 2025, with net debt of ~$1.7B and management targeting a longer-term mid-2x range while leaving room for opportunistic M&A.

Specialty and Infusion revenue grew 36% to $2.6B with script growth of ~30% (specialty above 30%, infusion mid-teens), and the company added 4 exclusive ultra-narrow LDDs, bringing the total LDD portfolio to 153.

Home and Community Pharmacy revenue declined 9% to $527M due to an expected ~$50M IRA impact and exits of uneconomic customers, with full-year 2026 IRA headwind expected at ~$175M for Home/Community and ~$181M for Specialty/Infusion, plus ~$250M from brand-to-generic conversions.
Home Healthcare revenue grew 49% to $266M, with the acquired Amedisys/LHC assets contributing $79M in revenue and ~$9M in adjusted EBITDA in Q1.
Management expects ~$500M of annual operating cash flow in 2026 (excluding Community Living), quarterly interest expense of ~$35M, and full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 5.2%–5.6%.

Pharmacy Solutions adjusted EBITDA grew 46% to $169M (5.3% margin, +70 bps) and Provider Services adjusted EBITDA grew 29% to $66M (14.9% margin, +10 bps), with the fee-for-service hub business (now 31 hub programs) growing 40%–50% year-over-year.
Third quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $321 million, up from $316 million in the second quarter.
The company executed a $100 million share and unit repurchase in the third quarter.
Third quarter distribution increased by 2.4%, or approximately 10% on an annualized basis, for Class A shares.
Gas gathering and processing throughput increased approximately 3% compared with the second quarter.
Full year 2025 capital expenditures are now expected to total approximately $270 million following suspension of the Capa gas plant.
Full year adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $1.245 billion to $1.255 billion, implying approximately 10% year-on-year EBITDA growth at the midpoint.
Gross adjusted EBITDA margin for the third quarter was maintained at approximately 80%, above the company's 75% target.
The company's leverage is currently at 3x, equal to its long-term leverage target of 3x adjusted EBITDA.

Full year adjusted free cash flow is expected to be approximately $760 million to $770 million, with excess adjusted free cash flow of approximately $140 million after fully funding targeted distributions.
Gas represents 75% of the company's revenues, and management expects gas volumes to continue to grow through at least 2027 driven by increasing gas-oil ratios.
Enact reported Q1 2026 adjusted operating income of $172 million or $1.21 per diluted share, up from $1.10 in Q1 2025 but down from $1.23 in Q4 2025, with adjusted operating ROE of 12.9%.
New insurance written (NIW) was $13 billion, down 11% sequentially but up 30% year-over-year, with primary insurance-in-force at $272 billion (up ~2% YoY).

The Board approved a 14% dividend increase from $0.21 to $0.24 per share (the fourth consecutive annual increase), and the company reaffirmed 2026 total capital return guidance of approximately $500 million.

Enact returned $123 million to shareholders in Q1 via $30 million in dividends and $93 million in buybacks (2.3 million shares at an average $40.66), with an additional 0.7 million shares repurchased for $30 million through April 30.
PMIERs sufficiency ratio was 162%, representing $1.9 billion above PMIERs requirements, with the third-party CRT program providing $1.9 billion of PMIERs capital credit.

Q1 losses were $37 million with a 15% loss ratio (vs. $18 million/7% in Q4 2025 and $31 million/12% in Q1 2025), including a $39 million net reserve release driven by favorable cures, while the claim rate on new delinquencies was maintained at 8%.

Persistency was 80% (flat sequentially, down 4 points YoY), supported by 58% of the portfolio carrying rates below 6% and only 21% of mortgages having rates at least 50 bps above March's 6.2% average.

New delinquencies were 13,600 (down from 13,700) with a 1.5% new delinquency rate, total delinquencies fell to 24,700, and cure rate rose 3 points sequentially to 54%; management indicated the 2.6% delinquency rate could tick up due to seasoning of higher-risk purchase-heavy books.
Net earned premium rate was 34.3 bps (down 0.5 bps sequentially) and base premium rate was 39.4 bps (down 0.2 bps), with management reaffirming flattish base premium rate guidance for full year 2026.

Investment income was $71 million (up 12% YoY) with a new money yield of 5% and average portfolio book yield of 4.5%, while operating expenses were $49 million (20% expense ratio) and full-year 2026 expense guidance of $215-$220 million (ex-reorg costs) was reaffirmed.
Fourth quarter 2025 revenue totaled $14.3 million, a decrease of $11.9 million or 46% compared to the fourth quarter of 2024.
Full year 2025 revenue increased to $86.2 million compared to $83.8 million in 2024, driven by strong performance in the first half of the year.
Full year 2025 cost of revenue increased 83% to $22 million from $12 million in 2024, causing gross margin to decline to 74.5% from 85.6% in 2024.
Net loss for full year 2025 was $5.1 million ($0.35 per share), an improvement of $667,000 compared to the net loss of $5.8 million ($0.41 per share) in 2024.

The company ended 2025 with $2.8 million in cash and $6.7 million availability under its borrowing facility, and subsequently received $6.2 million from a class action settlement and $3.3 million from a subordinated convertible note in January.
Inuvo acquired 83 new IntentKey clients in 2025 and entered 2026 with the strongest IntentKey sales pipeline to date.
Management expects Q1 2026 Platforms revenue to remain light with gradual recovery over the year, while forecasting strong double-digit growth in agencies and brands revenue for each quarter of 2026.
Management reiterated that the company could reach EBITDA breakeven at approximately $25 million in quarterly revenue.
A multiyear, multimillion-dollar government contract is reportedly weeks away from execution after clearing every procurement hurdle.

Fourth quarter 2025 operating expenses were $10.7 million, down more than 50% compared to Q4 2024, driven by a 60% year-over-year decrease in marketing expenses, and compensation expense is forecast to be lower in 2026 than in 2025.
Q3 2025 revenue reached a record $62.6 million, representing 20% year-over-year organic growth and 7% sequential quarterly growth.
Adjusted EBITDA was $16.2 million or 26% of revenue, up 23% sequentially quarter-over-quarter.
Cash increased to $73.9 million, up $27 million since year-end 2024 and $14.1 million since last quarter.
The company reiterates prior guidance of 45% or more year-over-year revenue growth in 2025 and anticipates potentially transformative growth in 2026.
Of the 8 big tech customers previously discussed, 6 are forecasted to grow next year, with several expected to grow quite substantially.

A $1.3 million investment in pretraining data capabilities has resulted in signed contracts expected to generate approximately $42 million in revenue, with an additional $26 million in contracts expected to sign soon.
Innodata Federal won an initial project with a new high-profile customer anticipated to result in approximately $25 million of revenue, mostly in 2026.

The company landed or expects to finalize shortly 5 additional big tech customers in Q3, with 3 of them positioned to allocate up to hundreds of millions of dollars annually to generative AI data and evaluation.
The company received verbal confirmation for a deal expected to potentially result in $6.5 million of revenue with one big tech customer.
The company anticipates incurring approximately $9.5 million in capability building investments in 2025, including $8.2 million of SG&A and direct operating costs and $1.3 million of CapEx.
Total revenues for the first 9 months of 2025 were $43.6 million, representing a 24% increase compared to the same period last year.
Q3 2025 total revenues were $17.9 million, reflecting a 1% decrease compared to Q3 2024.

For the 9 months ended September 30, 2025, revenues consisted of $18.6 million in Elfabrio sales to Chiesi, $15.4 million in Elelyso sales to Pfizer, and $9.1 million in Elelyso sales to Fiocruz in Brazil.
The IND for the Phase II clinical trial of PRX-115 was filed in October 2025 and became effective following the FDA's standard 30-day review period.
Research and development expenses for the 9 months ended September 30, 2025 totaled $13.9 million, an increase of 58% compared to $8.8 million for the prior year period.
